newsitem.title: USA: U.S. soybean crush sets record, may rise further.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soybean crush sets record, may rise further.

text.p: The pace of U.S. soybean crushings may rise from its already record level during the next few weeks and should remain strong at least until the end of the year, industry sources said.
The National Oilseed Processors Association reported on Thursday a weekly crush of 30.145 million bushels for the week to November 13, up from 29.898 million a week earlier.
"Any increase now is going to be fairly slow but I feel we could add another 500,000 to 800,000 (bushels)," one Indiana based industry source said.
They noted the weekly crush was now at around 87 percent of capacity, compared with 83 percent a year ago. Capacity has also increased during that period.
"We're crushing at a record level and still can't keep up with demand," another Indiana based crusher source said.
Another industry source said it was possible that one week it could even reach 32.0 million but others were doubtful that level could be achieved.
"You've got to figure in breakdowns. Eighty seven percent is hitting it pretty hard," one Tennessee soymeal broker said.
Crushers have been taking advantage of strong demand for soymeal from both the domestic and export markets, which has moved margins strongly into the black.
USDA reported earlier Friday that soymeal sales for the current marketing year stand at 2.25 million tonnes, up from 1.20 million at the same stage the previous year.
The rise reflects a sharp increase in sales to Asian consumers, including China, the Philippines and Thailand.
"Once the export valve shuts off things will change, but they (exports) should remain decent until the end of the year," the Tennessee source said.
"After that things become sketchy but nobody expects it (the market) to collapse," he added.
Industry sources also noted that demand from domestic soymeal consumers could rise over the next few weeks.
"Cold weather will probably spur feed demand more," one source said.
